text:
Sam: FYI reproduced an interop stall in staging: prefetch workers + eviction sweeps end up in a livelock under tight demote cadence. minimal trace attached.
Alisha: link?
Sam: gist: https://gist.github.com/repro-6145678901 (short stack + reproducible load script)
Ben: reading it now. looks like two things colliding: shard-level prefetch holds shard mutex while eviction holds tenant mutex. ordering flips across codepaths.
Chen: agreed. three candidate fixes: 1) global lock hierarchy (tenant before shard), 2) RPC-based graceful handoff (eviction asks prefetch to yield), 3) split locks / RW semantics so prefetch reads and eviction writes.
Maria: important constraint: we cannot increase tail latency on steady-state small requests. any solution that expands prefetch critical sections risks hurting 99.9th.
Kai: i'll run a microbench for options. will include workload variants: hotset zipf=0.9, 5k/50k prefixes, prefetch_concurrency 1/4/8, demote intervals 2/8/30s.
Alisha: operational concerns for RPC handoff: need idempotency, holder generation, and a backoff path if the prefetch is unresponsive. also consider auth/ACL surface but that's ok.
Ben: sketch for RPC handoff proto: ```rpc PrefixHandoff(Request) returns (HandoffReply);
message Request { string tenant; string prefix; string req_id; }
message HandoffReply { enum Status { OK=0; BUSY=1; NOT_FOUND=2; } Status status; uint64 holder_epoch; }
// handoff must be idempotent and tolerant of retries
```
Chen: if we add holder_epoch we can use compare-and-swap semantics when applying ownership at the eviction side. prevents dup-apply.
Sam: good. also think about transient duplicate ownership: prefetch might briefly still serve inflight reads while eviction thinks it owns. we must ensure KV apply is idempotent and fenced by epoch.
Maria: suggestion: attach a short lease window on ownership transfer so prefetch can gracefully stop accepting new work for that prefix for N ms. avoids races. but requires careful demote/rehype timing.
Ben: alternative optimistic path: eviction issues a non-blocking TRANSFER request and proceeds if no ACK in X ms, but records that it may have raced. then post-apply, background reconciliation checks for leftover owners and forces GC. tradeoff: complexity.
Kai: i'll include the optimistic variant in benches. measure how often races happen under different timing.
Alisha: telemetry to add: sampled "wait_chain_snapshot" when goroutine blocks > 5ms. include held locks and waiter stack. also emit a "handoff_event" metric with status codes and latencies.
Chen: for the shared-lock idea we need upgrade path from read->write. naive upgrade deadlocks when 2 readers try to upgrade. implement try_upgrade with randomized backoff or a ticketing upgrade queue. both add complexity.
Sam: short-term mitigation to avoid incidents: implement bounded-acquire in eviction path (acquire with timeout X ms), and if timed out, re-enqueue the prefix with exponential backoff. pair with temporary tighter eviction budget to prevent memory growth.
Maria: bounded-acquire buys safety but will delay eviction and could increase memory pressure; we should limit backoff ceiling and monitor mem growth. add an alert if tenant-residency > threshold.
Ben: note on correctness: whatever handoff path we choose, we must prove linearizability of prefix ownership with respect to apply operations. holder_epoch + request_id + idempotent apply gives us a good model.
Alisha: also add a lint rule and review checklist: any code touching prefix transfer must include a comment `// handoff-idempotent` and test the three failure modes (prefetch crash, network partition, duplicate request).
Kai: starting bench now. will post CSV + short summary in ~2h. including 95/99/99.9 and stall count.
Chen: i'll prototype try_upgrade RW lock and a safe upgrade test that simulates N concurrent readers all trying to upgrade. will put tests in `prefetch/locks_test.go`.
Sam: Ben, can you write a short doc listing failure scenarios for RPC handoff and how we detect & remediate each? include reconciliation steps.
Ben: yes. planning to sketch: (1) prefetch crash mid-handoff -> eviction should proceed if holder_epoch unchanged, (2) partial handoff -> reconciler scans prefixes with dual-owners and resolves by epoch, (3) duplicate handoff -> idempotent apply tolerates it.
evict-bot: created INF-2601: "staging: graceful-prefetch-evict-handoff investigation" and INF-2602: "telemetry: wait_chain_snapshot + handoff_event"
Sam: owners: Kai benches, Ben handoff failure doc + proto, Chen RW-lock prototype, Alisha telemetry + canary, Sam implement bounded-acquire patch. reconvene tomorrow 11am.
Maria: one more operational note: include a canary gating rule that fails deploy if staging stall_rate > 0.05% for 30m. better to be conservative.
Alisha: will add canary and PR lint.
Kai: bench infra running. will iterate if we need longer runs.
Sam: thanks. keep the thread small and paste PRs/CSVs. we'll include results in the postmortem doc.
